citations.narrative:
The facility has exceeded the maximum number of animals allowed on their license without prior authorization. The
license has authorized up to 850 animals. The routine inspection conducted on 30-September-2026 identified that the
facility currently houses approximately 1039 animals. The USDA license authorizes a specific number of animals to
ensure that the facility and personnel possess adequate facilities, employees and knowledge to provide sufficient
husbandry to the regulated animals. The number of non-compliances documented on the routine inspection report
demonstrates that exceeding the approved animal numbers has resulted in the facilities inability to properly care for the
animal causing serious welfare concerns.
The facility must obtain authorization to increase the approved maximum number of animals or reduce the number of
regulated animals to a number which is under the maximum threshold authorized under the current license.

The second building housing approximately 268 animals is not being adequately maintained in good repair, is not
structurally sound, and does not protect the animals from injury:
-In the far side of the building, there is a section of the ceiling that is caving in onto a row of enclosures housing some
animals and enclosures that could potentially house animals. The ceiling appears to be caving in about 1 foot with a
noticeable bend in the structure.
-In the majority of enclosures, there were jagged edges found in the metal feeders and dust baths.
-There were various sharp points on metal wiring of the enclosure fronts, doors, and walls of enclosures.
-A few enclosures contained floors that were falling apart due to rust forming sharp points.
Failure to maintain housing facilities in structurally sound condition and in good repair could result in the ceiling falling
onto the enclosures causing injury to the regulated animals. Jagged edges could also result in injury to the regulated
animals. The facility must be constructed of such material and of such strength as appropriate for the animals involved.
Correct by ensuring housing facilities shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to protect the
animals from injury and to contain the animals.

In the second building housing 268 animals, the facility is not adequately cleaning the premises:
-Multiple enclosures were observed with clumps of hair from the animals trapped in the wire fencing in both the front and
rear of the enclosures. Hair was also seen caught on the automatic watering lines. Unused enclosures and runs that
attach multiple enclosures for breeding contain multiple cobwebs trapping debris. Spaces in this building not currently
being used to house animals are cluttered with accumulation of trash, dust, debris, soiled animal bedding, cobwebs,
equipment, and miscellaneous items.
-Most of the ceiling panels in the second building have areas of severe accumulations of dark brown, black, and white
staining.
Failure to adequately clean the animal enclosures and the premises can lead to illness, transmission of diseases, and
attract unwanted pests. The facility must ensure that the premises are kept clean and in good repair to protect the animals
from injury to facilitate the prescribed husbandry practices set forth in this subpart.

An effective pest control method is not being utilized at the facility. There were numerous spiders located throughout the
facility, with numerous spiders found in close proximity to the animals. Failure to ensure facility is free from pests could
result in injury or disease transmission to the regulated animals. A safe and effective program for the control of insects,
ectoparasites, and avian and mammalian pests shall be established and maintained.

There are an insufficient number of adequately trained employees to carry out the level of husbandry practices and care
required by the Animal Welfare Act. There is one full-time employee, one full-time assistant, and a part-time assistant
responsible for the care of approximately 1039 animals at this facility. There is a history of numerous and severe non-
compliances identified pertaining to the cleaning, sanitation, watering, and veterinary care. The majority of non-
compliances identified during this inspection were observed in building 2.
The issues seen are consistent with shortages of personnel. Insufficient personnel can lead to a failure in maintenance of
the facility, delayed care for the animals, and unnecessary suffering and health concerns for the animals. The facility must
ensure a sufficient number of adequately trained employees are utilized to maintain the professionally acceptable level of
husbandry practices set forth in this subpart. Such practices shall be under the supervision of an animal caretaker who
has a background in animal husbandry or care.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the Facility Representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture

Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
